assumptions: No structured SpecJson state list was provided; the model names twelve modes from the NL-described operating branches and uses the root name LNGShipEMS from the summary domain.

The model is a condition-classification abstraction: forced guard transitions reselect the active dispatch state from current PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity inputs rather than modeling event-memory hysteresis.
The NL mentions twelve finite states but gives fewer explicit branch names. ZeroLoad_NoRES is included as a twelfth zero-load/no-renewable branch to preserve the stated cardinality.
eng3_Pmax is treated as the LNG/primary thermal capacity bound because the NL cites it as an engine capacity bound while also stating LNG is used before diesel units.
Pd2max is introduced as the DG2 capacity bound so the DG1/DG2 last-priority and all-thermal overload conditions can be expressed.
Pgmax is treated as the suitable battery discharge capability and as the base of the Pgmax/5 low-SoC charge margin; the NL does not define a separate battery discharge maximum.
A low-SoC threshold of 0.2 is used for branch separation because the NL mentions low-SoC branches but only explicitly specifies the full threshold 0.95.

Load cut-in/cut-out variables are declared because the NL says commands apply to generating units and loads, but no concrete load-shedding condition is specified; cmd_load_cutout remains inactive in this initial abstraction.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, the EMS serves all ship demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Dispatch follows RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable, LNG before diesel units.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
DG1/DG2 only as the last priority after LNG.

canonical_scenario_results.description: default-init probe with default PL=0 and no RES: EMS should classify zero-load/no-renewable operation with no charge, spare, or illegal flag.
canonical_scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_no_res_classification

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: with PL=0, positive RES, and SoC below 0.95, renewable production should be sent to battery charging.
canonical_scenario_results.name: zero_load_res_charges_battery

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: with PL=0, positive RES, and SoC exactly 0.95, renewable production should become spare power, not battery charge.
canonical_scenario_results.name: zero_load_full_soc_res_to_spare

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when RES covers positive load and SoC is below 0.95, load is served by RES and surplus charges the battery.
canonical_scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_charges_battery_below_full

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: when RES covers positive load and SoC is exactly 0.95, surplus RES should be spare rather than charging.
canonical_scenario_results.name: res_covers_load_spare_at_full_soc

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: when RES is below load, SoC is exactly suitable at 0.2, and deficit equals Pgmax, batteries should cover the deficit.
canonical_scenario_results.name: battery_assist_at_soc_and_pgmax_boundary

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: with suitable SoC but deficit greater than battery limit and within LNG capacity, LNG should cut in before diesel units.
canonical_scenario_results.name: lng_covers_normal_after_battery_limit

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start low-SoC probe: when LNG can cover deficit plus Pgmax/5 charging margin, EMS should request LNG power and charge the battery by Pgmax/5.
canonical_scenario_results.name: lng_low_soc_charge_margin

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when suitable-SoC deficit exceeds LNG capacity but is within LNG plus DG1 capacity, DG1 should cut in while DG2 remains cut out.
canonical_scenario_results.name: dg1_covers_normal_after_lng_limit

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start low-SoC probe: when diesel stage is needed and Pd1max/10 margin fits within LNG plus DG1 capacity, EMS should charge by Pd1max/10.
canonical_scenario_results.name: dg1_low_soc_charge_margin

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: when suitable-SoC deficit exceeds LNG plus DG1 but is within DG2 addition, DG2 should cut in as last-priority thermal unit.
canonical_scenario_results.name: dg2_covers_normal_after_dg1_limit

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start illegal-overload probe: when demand exceeds all RES and thermal resources, all thermal units should be active and remaining lack covered by battery discharge.
canonical_scenario_results.name: extreme_overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-transition probe: from the illegal overload leaf, changing inputs to PL=0 with positive RES and SoC at 0.95 must globally reclassify to zero-load spare; if wildcard forced guards are missing this stays illegal.
canonical_scenario_results.name: forced_reclassification_illegal_to_zero_load_spare

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-transition probe: from a RES-covering leaf, changed inputs with RES below load, suitable SoC, and deficit equal to Pgmax must globally reclassify to battery assist; if wildcard forced transitions are missing it remains in the old RES state.
canonical_scenario_results.name: forced_reclassification_res_charge_to_battery_assist

canonical_scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start forced-transition probe: from a DG2 thermal leaf, changed inputs where RES covers load and SoC is at 0.95 must globally reclassify to RES spare; this catches missing wildcard forced reclassification from non-RES modes.
canonical_scenario_results.name: forced_reclassification_dg2_to_res_covers_spare

finding_summaries.summary: Core NL dispatch rules are represented with reasonable fidelity: RES coverage, SoC 0.95 charge/spare threshold, battery assist, LNG-before-diesel priority, DG1/DG2 escalation, and the illegal overload diagnostic branch are all present.

evidence: Variables include `PL`, `Ppv`, `Pw`, `SoC`, `eng3_Pmax`, `Pgmax`, `Pd1max`, `Pd2max`, `Pgen_req`, `Pbat_discharge`, `Pbat_charge`, `Pspare`, and generator command variables.
Grounding map marks core state, guard, transition, and action elements as required and grounded to the NL.
finding_summaries.summary: The model covers the main EMS components and target outputs: PV/WEC renewable inputs, load, SoC, LNG/DG capacity bounds, requested generation, battery charge/discharge, spare power, and generator cut-in/cut-out commands.

evidence: DSL has `LNG_Covers_LowSoC_ChargeMargin` for `SoC < 0.2` and `DG1_LowSoC_ChargeMargin` for `SoC < 0.2`.
DSL has `DG2_Covers_Normal` only for `SoC >= 0.2`.

NL says low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including `Pgmax/5` in an LNG-covered case and `Pd1max/10` in later diesel-generator cases; this leaves DG2 low-SoC behavior under-specified or uncovered.
finding_summaries.summary: Low-SoC diesel/DG2 coverage appears incomplete: the model includes LNG low-SoC and DG1 low-SoC charging-margin branches, but no explicit low-SoC DG2 charging-margin or low-SoC DG2 normal branch before overload.

evidence: NL says the EMS issues cut-in and cut-out commands for generating units and loads.
Every listed state action sets `cmd_load_cutin = 1` and `cmd_load_cutout = 0`.
No load-shedding or load command transition condition is modeled; the grounding assumptions acknowledge no concrete load-shedding condition was specified.
finding_summaries.summary: Load cut-in/cut-out behavior is mostly a placeholder: the DSL declares load command outputs but keeps `cmd_load_cutin = 1` and `cmd_load_cutout = 0` in all states, including overload.

evidence: DSL transition to `Extreme_Overload_Illegal` uses `PL > Ppv + Pw && PL - Ppv - Pw > eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max`.
`Extreme_Overload_Illegal.enter` sets all thermal cut-in commands to 1 and `illegal_state = 1`.
NL states the overload completion state is illegal and shall never occur in practice, but also describes the all-thermal plus battery behavior if extreme demand occurs.
finding_summaries.summary: The illegal overload state is reachable, but it is explicitly marked diagnostic/illegal and follows the NL-specified fallback of activating all thermal units and covering the lack by battery discharge; this is not treated as blocking under the admitted exceptional-branch guidance.

evidence: Inspect summary reports `n_transitions_forced = 144`, `n_events = 0`, and `n_transitions_normal = 1`.
DSL uses repeated `! * -> State : if [...]` classification transitions.
Source assumptions state the model is a condition-classification abstraction rather than event-memory hysteresis.
finding_summaries.summary: The FSM is implemented as a combinational classifier with global forced transitions from every state to every dispatch state. This matches the stated abstraction but produces high transition count and limited temporal/mode semantics.

evidence: Design diagnostics classify warnings as advisory with `blocking_count = 0`.
External input role ledger identifies `PL`, `Ppv`, `Pw`, `SoC`, `eng3_Pmax`, `Pgmax`, `Pd1max`, and `Pd2max` as external input candidates.
Output variables such as `Pgen_req`, `Pbat_discharge`, `Pbat_charge`, and `Pspare` are NL-returned outputs, so lack of guard references is not by itself a defect.
finding_summaries.summary: No unjustified warning-driven repair is evident. The many unwritten-read and unreferenced-variable warnings are consistent with external input and pure output roles rather than necessarily requiring model changes.

evidence: Grounding assumptions introduce `Pd2max`, interpret `eng3_Pmax` as LNG/primary thermal capacity, and use an inferred low-SoC threshold of `0.2` not explicitly given in the NL.

finding_summaries.summary: Estimated NFRR tier is T2 within-scope candidate, not T3/T4. The candidate is usable and substantially grounded, but quality is capped by inferred constants/variables, limited five-component evidence, combinational classifier structure, and minor branch coverage uncertainty.
